title: More Than One
label: ch:ur-more-than-one
canDo: I can make a noun plural, and I can make it plural before a postposition, which is the one ending in Urdu that is never ambiguous.

payoff.summary: No noun in this book had ever been more than one. The four-cell table closes, two of its cells collide on purpose, and ہم gives the track its first plural pronoun and its first plural possessive.
payoff.note: The plural of a masculine -ا noun is spelled exactly like its oblique singular, and the chapter teaches the collision rather than hiding it: the postposition is what settles the reading.
